title: Towards a Visual-Language Foundation Model for Computational Pathology
abstract: The vast majority of artificial intelligence (AI) models for computational pathology (CPath) are trained in a supervised manner on datasets with restricted access, and hence may not generalize to new tasks or unseen data. Here we present CONCH (CONtrastive learning from Captions for Histopathology), a vision-language foundation model for CPath developed using diverse sources of histopathology images, biomedical text, and over 1.17 million image-caption pairs via task-agnostic pretraining. Evaluated on a suite of 14 diverse benchmarks ranging from patch-level to slide-level tasks including classification, segmentation, captioning, text-to-image and image-to-text retrieval, CONCH represents a substantial improvement over prior art and enables machine learning-based workflows requiring minimal or no further supervised fine-tuning. To facilitate further research in CPath, we release CONCH under a research-use license.
